blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (No way back from the switch to Paylane) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (A failed or missed nightly settlement goes unnoticed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (or feature flag) that selects the provider, so card payments can go back to Stripe without a release; keep the Stripe account open until Paylane has run in production for an agreed period, and write the rollback procedure in the design.
findings.title: No way back from the switch to Paylane

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Give the worker structured start/end logs, metrics (payments fetched, matched, unmatched, duration, last success time) and an alert when the job fails or has not succeeded in 24 hours; state how a missed night is re-run without settling a payment twice.
findings.title: A failed or missed nightly settlement goes unnoticed

findings.evidence: Every card payment SHALL be authorized and captured through Paylane once the change is deployed.
findings.location: specs/payments/spec.md#Requirement: Card payments go through Paylane
findings.recommendation: Specify in the design a timeout on every Paylane call from `services/checkout` and from the worker, bounded retries with backoff, and an idempotency key on authorize/capture so a retry cannot charge a card twice; define what the customer sees when Paylane does not answer.
findings.title: No timeout, retry or idempotency policy for Paylane calls

findings.evidence: - **THEN** it is written to the `unmatched_payments` table
findings.recommendation: Emit a metric and an alert (or a report to the team that handles payments) when `unmatched_payments` receives rows, with the payment identifier and amount, so captured money without an order is acted on.
findings.title: Unmatched payments are written to a table nobody watches

findings.recommendation: State that the Paylane endpoint, API key and the worker schedule are read from the environment (Kubernetes secrets/config), never hard-coded or logged.
findings.title: Paylane configuration and credentials are not specified
